extracted.intended_audience: early-career tenure‑track faculty (Assistant/Associate professors) and departmental nominators involved in Packard Fellowship nominations
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare and submit a university‑limited nomination package for the David and Lucile Packard Foundation Packard Fellowships, meeting eligibility, formatting, and content requirements and addressing the Foundation's selection priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and award terms
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Fellowship provides largely unrestricted funding to take risks and pursue new avenues of research. Budget detail: $175K per year for five years; indirect costs at 10%.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional nomination limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Cornell is limited to submitting 2 nominees (including Ithaca). Chairpersons/Institute-Center Directors/Division Heads may submit no more than one (1) nomination from their department/division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An internal selection process will be coordinated because of the institutional cap; nominators must follow internal deadlines. Example internal deadline on this page: January 5, 2025 at 11:59 PM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program focus and funding priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: To support the nation's most promising early career professors to pursue their science and engineering research with few funding restrictions. The Foundation is looking for conceptually revolutionary big ideas that have the potential of being widely adopted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding priorities emphasize core fundamental (not applied) research in many disciplines. The program is not interested in funding clinical or social science research, research associated with the design and construction of large national facilities, or projects that are extensions/components of large-scale ongoing research programs. The Fellowships are directed to less generously supported fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary selection criteria: recommendation letter and research importance
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation letter (first) and importance/impact of research (second) are the 2 most important evaluation criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation letters must be written by prominent figures in the candidate's field, should understand the candidate's work very well, and be able to say that the research is important and the candidate is a leader in the field. Ideally at least one letter writer is not in a supervisory role (not required but suggested). Recommenders who are themselves Packard Fellows, or mentored Packard Fellows, are highly regarded as letter writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation letter writer characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Letter writers should be prominent figures who understand the candidate's work well and can attest to the research's importance and the candidate's leadership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At least one writer ideally is not a supervisor. Writers who are Packard Fellows or who have mentored Packard Fellows are highly regarded. The letter is considered the single most important element in evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance/impact of research
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation places high weight on the importance and potential impact of the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation seeks conceptually revolutionary big ideas with potential for wide adoption. Emphasize why the research matters in a broad scientific context rather than framing as an extension of existing large programs or applied/clinical goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication track record
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication track record is important to be able to be recognized and labeled as an expert in a field for a specific body of work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present key publications that establish expertise and impact. Track record helps reviewers recognize the candidate as an authority in a specific research area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previous funding and awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Having previous funding and/or awards can be perceived as a positive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List current external support and notable awards; however, the Fellowship favors early‑career investigators who are not already well established or generously funded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: appointment dates and status
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible candidates are in the first tenure‑track faculty appointments, as Assistant or Associate Professors. Their initial faculty appointments must have begun no earlier than May 31, 2023, and no later than May 31, 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates must have PI status, lead independent groups, and have dedicated lab space. The program is intended for highly creative early career researchers; faculty who are well established and well‑funded are less likely to receive the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplines considered / exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplines considered include physics, chemistry, mathematics, biology, astronomy, computer science, earth science, ocean science, and all branches of engineering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program does not consider candidates engaged in social sciences, clinical research, research associated with design/construction of large national facilities, or projects that are extensions/components of large-scale ongoing research programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research statement content and audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Research statement should include background information, specific aims, describe why the research is important and outline the general goals for the next five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pitch an appealing idea around an important topic. Write the research statement for a broader scientific audience: reviewers will be seasoned scientists outside your field of work. Check the Current Advisory Panel Members, select those closer to your field, and write so they will understand and appreciate your work. The statement should be credible but extensive preliminary data is not required. For figures/images/references include these separately on a third page.

rubrics_metrics.name: 30‑line scientific abstract requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: 30‑lines scientific abstract explaining the qualifications of the applicant and fit of the project for this funding mechanism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract should concisely explain applicant qualifications and why the proposed project fits the Fellowship's goals; adhere to the 30‑line limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letter of nomination requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Letter of nomination from the Department Chairperson/Division Head/Institute or Center Director detailing why the candidate should be considered (1-2 pages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This nomination letter is part of the institutional selection process and should explain why the institution supports this nominee and why they are an excellent candidate for the Packard Fellowship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosketch and current support disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Biosketch with the nominee's appointment date (month/day/year). List all current external support and potential overlap with the Packard project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include appointment start date explicitly and clearly disclose any overlapping projects or support that could present overlap with the proposed Packard work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting, file composition, and naming conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Margins should be at least one inch and font size no less than 12 point. Submit items in the order listed as one PDF document using the naming convention PI last name-first initial_Packard2026.pdf (example: Smith-J_Packard2026.pdf).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specified ordering and file naming exactly. Figures, images, or references should be placed separately on a third page as instructed. Submit by the stated internal deadline (example: January 5, 2025 at 11:59 PM) to the institutional link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal submission process and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Cornell internal deadline and submission link requirements apply (example internal deadline: January 5, 2025 at 11:59 PM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of institutional nominee limits, adhere to the internal timeline and coordinate with department/institute leaders for nomination. All materials must be bundled and uploaded to the institutional submission link by the internal deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer composition and audience expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fellowship Advisory Panel comprises senior scientists (list provided); reviewers will be seasoned scientists outside your field of work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because reviewers may be from other fields (e.g., computer scientists reviewing biological proposals), craft explanations at a level accessible to non‑specialists while conveying the novelty and importance of the work. Consulting the Current Advisory Panel Members may help tailor the statement.
